clue.text: Drug problem starts to attract troublesome element

parts.note: a drug habit is an addiction

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: first letter A
first letter T

explanation.surface: An addiction begins to draw in a disruptive crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' looks like a chemistry term or a member of a troublesome group, but it is the definition, in the sense of being in your element.
explanation.definitionFit: Your element is the natural surroundings where you thrive, which is what a habitat is for a creature.

clue.text: Absolutely determined that Man will be proven innocent ultimately

parts.note: that man will be is he'll be, written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the final letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: last letter N
last letter T

explanation.surface: Someone resolutely insisting a man will eventually be cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital M on 'Man' suggests the Isle of Man; it is just a man, so 'that Man will be' becomes HE'LL BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent means recklessly set on doing something, an idiom for being utterly resolved.

clue.text: Complain about hospital following drill

indicators.note: following says the letters for about and hospital come after the word for drill

parts.note: a bit is the boring tool fitted to a drill
C stands for circa, Latin for about
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Moaning about a hospital after a fire drill or some dental work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'following' puts C and H below BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To bitch is an informal verb meaning to grumble or moan spitefully about something.

clue.text: Suspect senator's attempting to overthrow government?

indicators.note: suspect is read as an adjective meaning dodgy, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: read as senator is, so the anagram fodder is the word senator, with the 's a link

explanation.surface: A dubious politician is plotting a coup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a verb, accusing the senator; it is the anagram signal on SENATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying your country, notably by plotting to overthrow its rulers; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: London Underground entrance about to close early

indicators.note: close early means the word stops before its last letter
about means turned round, so the word for entrance is read backwards

parts.note: a debut is a first entrance onto the stage or into society

explanation.surface: A tube station entrance is about to shut ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a station way in; it is DEBUT, which 'about' turns into TUBED, and 'close early' cuts the last letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tube is the everyday nickname for the London Underground railway network.

clue.text: Wary of running feud disrupting almost all aid

indicators.note: disrupting says the jumbled feud breaks into the shortened word for aid
almost all says the word for aid loses its final letter

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: running means the letters of feud are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cautious about a continuing quarrel that is upsetting nearly every bit of assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wary of' is the definition: heedful takes 'of' after it just as wary does.
explanation.definitionFit: Being heedful of something means paying careful attention to it, close to being cautious or on guard about it.

clue.text: Stranded in the Atacama desert?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: left stuck and helpless, an idiom from boats left on shore
second meaning, read literally: the Atacama is a lofty and extremely arid desert in Chile

explanation.walkthrough: The Atacama in northern Chile is one of the driest places on Earth and much of it lies at altitude, so the idiom fits it word for word; the question mark flags the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being abandoned without help or resources happens also to describe a plateau desert's altitude and aridity.

clue.text: Say nothing about lawyers supporting mass prohibition

indicators.note: about means going round, so EG and O wrap round the rest

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means in 'say, a dog'

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the lawyers under the mass

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass
the Bar is the collective name for barristers
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about attorneys backing a large-scale ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say nothing' reads as a single instruction to keep mum; it splits into EG (say) and O (nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade with a particular country.

clue.text: Make official warning to store belonging to African country

indicators.note: to store means to keep inside, so the Mali letters go inside the warning

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
Mali's means belonging to Mali, the West African country

explanation.surface: A government formally cautions a shop owned by an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the shout a golfer gives to warn people a ball is heading their way.
explanation.definitionFit: To formalise an arrangement is to give it official status or a fixed legal form.

clue.text: Character that features in epistolary novel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a symbol of the alphabet
second meaning: an epistolary novel is told through correspondence, so each such item of post features in it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' and 'novel' together suggest a fictional person; the first sense is an alphabet symbol and the second is an item of correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a written symbol of the alphabet and a written message sent by post.

clue.text: Rubbish broadcaster on radio set fire to a hidden mike

indicators.note: on radio says the words are heard, not read: lit a, said in a British accent, sounds like the word for rubbish

parts.note: set fire to means lit, so these words give LIT A
a bug is a concealed microphone

explanation.surface: A bad broadcaster on the wireless torched a concealed microphone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish broadcaster' looks like an insult to a radio presenter; it is someone who scatters rubbish. In a non-rhotic British accent 'lit a' and 'litter' sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug throws rubbish around in public places, literally strewing or broadcasting it like seed.

clue.text: Cap on splitting money in speculative venture

indicators.note: splitting says the word for on goes inside, dividing the word for the stake

parts.note: a bet is a stake of money risked on an outcome
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A limit placed on dividing up the funds put into a risky enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' reads as a limit on spending, but it is the definition: a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A beret is a soft round flat hat, one kind of cap worn on the head.

clue.text: What stops triumph over order?

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the reversed word fills the middle of the other

parts.note: to best someone is to triumph over them

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the word for what is read backwards

parts.note: eh is a way of saying what? when you have not heard

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what prevents victory over a command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What?' is a request to repeat yourself, the same as 'Eh?'. The question mark dresses the whole clue as a riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at someone's behest means doing it at their command or instruction.

clue.text: Cost of moving goods vehicle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the charge for transporting goods
second meaning: a wheeled conveyance, such as a horse-drawn coach or railway coach

explanation.surface: The price of shifting freight by van.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a transport charge in commerce and a passenger coach on wheels or rails.

clue.text: Person helping to write out names in USA

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A ghostwriter spells out names in America.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a secretary or assistant who takes dictation or copies manuscripts for someone else.

clue.text: Arrested man reversed charges and called informally

indicators.note: charges means loads or fills, so the arrest word takes the turned-round man inside it

parts.note: nicked is British slang for arrested

indicators.note: reversed says the word man is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before reversal

explanation.surface: A detained man reverses the accusations and is given a casual label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' looks like the police accusations that follow an arrest; it is the containment signal, as a gun is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname is an informal name, so to be nicknamed is to be called something casually rather than by your real name.

clue.text: Cold and unappetising article in French toast sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between two parts, so the toast word encloses the article

parts.note: cheers is what you say when raising a glass as a toast
les is the French plural definite article

explanation.surface: French toast sandwiches with a grammar word inside are cold and unappealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French toast' reads as the eggy breakfast dish; split it so 'French' goes with 'article' and 'toast' gives CHEERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerless describes something dreary and bleak, offering no comfort or warmth.

clue.text: Exclude some testimony that's been retracted

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the hidden run is read backwards
some says only part of the next word is wanted

parts.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: Leave out part of the evidence that a witness has since withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, which is the same as excluding it.

clue.text: I speak badly of key individual?

parts.note: to slander someone is to speak falsely and damagingly about them

explanation.surface: A confession that the speaker bad-mouths the most important person.
explanation.walkthrough: A key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys, so a 'key individual' is someone living on one; the question mark marks the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: An islander is a person who lives on an island, and a key is a small coral island.

clue.text: Counter had fine cheese

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: counter means running the opposite way, so the word for had is read backwards

parts.note: had, as in had a meal, means ate

explanation.surface: The deli counter stocked some excellent cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a shop counter in this cheesy scene; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined cheese from Greece, made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Missionary position adopted by naked men

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by, so the job word goes inside the stripped word
naked means stripped, so the word for men loses its outer letters

parts.note: males are men
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a sex position taken up by men with no clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missionary position' reads as one phrase; the definition is 'Missionary' alone and 'position' is POST.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a leading early Christian missionary, sent out to spread the faith.

clue.text: Collected head of state in navy vessel at sea

indicators.note: in says the head of state's letters go inside the navy vessel letters
at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the British head of state

explanation.surface: A leader is picked up and placed aboard a warship out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' looks like a call for the first letter of state, but it means the Queen, ER for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone collected is calm and composed; nerveless describes a person who stays cool and shows no nerves.

clue.text: Very dangerous nurse leads chase

indicators.note: leads means goes in front, so the nurse letters come first

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
a grave situation is very serious or perilous

explanation.surface: A risky pursuit led by a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chase' looks like a pursuit; it is the metalworking verb meaning to engrave.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase metal is to decorate it by cutting or embossing patterns, which is to engrave it.

clue.text: Part of brazen campaign pitch

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a shameless political drive's sales pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' reads as a sales pitch; it is the verb, to pitch tents.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch camp or a tent is to set up a camp, so to encamp is to pitch.

clue.text: Broadcast again revolved around argument that's more bigoted

indicators.note: around says the turned word goes round the word for argument
revolved means turned round, so the word for broadcast again is read backwards

parts.note: a show broadcast again was rerun or reran
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A repeated programme went round and round a dispute that is increasingly intolerant.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow-minded people are bigoted, so narrower in that sense means more intolerant of other views.

clue.text: Group blocking postgraduate qualification for medicine man

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, so the word for group goes inside the degree

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
a gang is a group of people

explanation.surface: A clique stops a faculty awarding a higher degree to a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: MGANGA is a Swahili word used in East Africa for a traditional healer or witch doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A mganga is an East African traditional healer, the kind of figure called a medicine man.

clue.text: Supply only new material

indicators.note: supply is read as supple-ly, in a flexible way, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Provide nothing but fresh fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb meaning provide; read as supple plus -ly, it says the letters bend into new shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fibre and the fabric woven from it, used for stockings and clothing.

clue.text: Protection provided by English and American soldiers

parts.note: GIs are US soldiers

explanation.surface: Allied troops from Britain and the US give cover.
explanation.walkthrough: EGIS is the American spelling of aegis.
explanation.definitionFit: Under someone's aegis means under their protection or sponsorship; the word is the shield of Zeus.

clue.text: Warning from porter perhaps emptied restaurant

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an example of ale

indicators.note: emptied says the inside of the word is removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters R and T

explanation.surface: A caution from a hotel porter after the dining room has cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' suggests a doorman, but it is the dark beer, and 'perhaps' marks it as an example of ale.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a signal that warns people of danger, such as a flood alert.

clue.text: Made known criminal's last dealings subject to review

indicators.note: subject to review means up for reworking, so these letters are rearranged
last asks for the final letter of the word criminal

parts.note: last letter of criminal gives L
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A crook's latest transactions are being investigated and exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To signal something is to communicate it, so signalled means communicated or indicated to others.

clue.text: Have Post Office review following disappearance of article

indicators.note: says the article is taken away from the review word, which then follows the office

parts.note: to review a case is to assess it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The postal service gets an inspection after a missing item.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to own or hold it, the same as to have it.

clue.text: Royal Navy pilot admits being less lenient

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the navy letters go inside the word for pilot

parts.note: to pilot a craft is to steer it

explanation.surface: A navy aviator confesses to being stricter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' reads as an airman confessing; it is a verb, to steer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sterner person is harsher and stricter, the opposite of being more forgiving or easy-going.
